answer: Session keys rotate after every accepted task and each rotation needs a signed pulse from the live key holder, so a clone has to keep a real process running to stay payable. Payment sits in escrow until finality, which turns a batch of fake workers into a slow dune of escrowed money. Duplicates are caught on replay, not by name. The velvet front end hides none of it: one clone costs a key cycle, a month of escrow and a pulse every rotation.
